comments.content: The layout's main container uses `mx-auto w-full ... px-3 py-5` without a `max-w-*` constraint. Since this page now delegates its outer padding to the layout (removing the prior `px-4 py-8` wrapper), the content will span the full viewport width on large screens. Consider adding `max-w-7xl` (or similar) so the content is constrained and `mx-auto` actually centers it, otherwise wide-screen layouts become overly stretched.
comments.existing_code: <div className="mx-auto w-full min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col px-3 py-5 sm:px-6 lg:px-8">

comments.content: This refactor removes the non-compliant clamp()/custom breakpoints (good), but it also removed ALL horizontal/vertical padding from the card-paper header. Previously it had p-[clamp(...)] plus mobile padding overrides. Without any p-* utility, the centered heading and paragraph text will render flush against the card border with no breathing room. Keep standard padding utilities (e.g. p-6 sm:p-10 sm:pb-8 sm:pt-12 or similar) instead of dropping padding entirely.

comments.content: The nav grid is declared as `md:grid-cols-5` (5 columns), but after removing the 'Song library' and 'Grades' links and replacing with a single 'Teacher toolbox' link, the nav now only contains 4 items. This leaves an empty column and makes the footer navigation asymmetric on md+ screens. Consider changing to `md:grid-cols-4` to match the number of links.
comments.suggestion_code: <nav className="grid grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-4 gap-6 mb-10" aria-label="Main navigation">
comments.existing_code: <nav className="grid grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-5 gap-6 mb-10" aria-label="Main navigation">

comments.content: Inconsistent indentation introduced by this diff: the first `section` (line 54) sits at 6-space indent, while all subsequent sections ("Design proof points", "Value proposition", "The story") still retain the old 8-space nesting indent from the removed container divs. This creates an inconsistent JSX tree structure inside the fragment and should be realigned to a single consistent level.

Inconsistency in the chart-5 token between light and dark modes. Light mode `--chart-5: var(--cast-mr-puddles-color)` resolves to #4f5fa0 (purple), but dark mode `--chart-5: var(--cast-puddles-color)` resolves to #4fa0c9 (light blue) — two different cast characters producing a completely different hue. Every other dark-mode chart token (chart-1/2/3) uses the `-soft` variant of the SAME base color as light mode, so chart-5 breaks that pattern. Render chart-5 from the same base token in both modes (e.g., keep it aligned with `--cast-mr-puddles-color` family) so series 5 has consistent meaning across themes.

Dark-mode `--chart-4: var(--navy-muted)` resolves to #e8dcc8 because the `.dark` block redefines `--navy-muted` to a cream/light tone (inverting the navy family). This nearly collides with `--chart-1: var(--gold-soft)` = #f0d88a — both are light warm cream tones, so series 1 and series 4 become hard to distinguish in dark charts. Consider mapping the dark chart-4 to a token that stays a distinct dark series color (or a soft variant of a different base hue) rather than a once-navy token that was inverted.

The Card component already applies `bg-card text-card-foreground` by default (see components/ui/card.tsx base class: `flex flex-col gap-(--card-spacing) rounded-xl border bg-card ... text-card-foreground`). Adding them here is redundant dead code and only adds noise to the className. The same redundant addition appears on all 5 changed Cards in this file (lines 171, 194, 247, 276, 294). Remove `bg-card text-card-foreground` from the className.
comments.suggestion_code: <Card className="material-surface material-cardboard-paper relative gap-3 overflow-hidden py-4">
comments.existing_code: <Card className="material-surface material-cardboard-paper relative gap-3 overflow-hidden py-4 bg-card text-card-foreground">

comments.content: The header now uses `bg-primary`, which maps to `--primary: var(--navy-deep)`. In dark mode `--navy-deep` is redefined to `#fefce8` (cream, see globals.css line 169), so the header background inverts to cream in dark mode. The project design rules explicitly require brand surfaces (header/footer/hero) to be solid navy `#1e2a38` and "NEVER inverted in dark mode". Using `bg-primary` violates this contract. Prefer a brand-navy surface token (or a dedicated non-inverting navy class) so the header stays navy in both themes.
comments.existing_code: <header className="bg-primary border-b border-primary-foreground/10 sticky top-0 z-40">

comments.content: The WorkingWallNote heading prop renders as a CardTitle ("Plan with intention"), and then the Badge immediately below repeats the same text. This duplicates the phrase "Plan with intention" twice in the same card. The original code used the Badge as a kicker and a distinct sentence as the title. Set the heading prop to the actual statement (e.g. the "Build learning around familiar songs..." sentence) and keep the Badge as a label, or drop the redundant Badge, so the text isn't repeated.

<WorkingWallNote fastener="pin" heading="Plan with intention" className="bg-muted">
        <Badge variant="secondary" className="w-fit">
          Plan with intention
        </Badge>

comments.content: Using a raw arrow character inside a Button violates the project's icon convention. Per the design rules, icons inside buttons should be lucide-react components with data-icon="inline-end" (e.g. <ArrowRight data-icon="inline-end" />), not a styled text arrow span. Use an icon for consistency with the other buttons on the page.

The `bg-card text-card-foreground` classes are redundant — the shadcn Card already applies `bg-card ... text-card-foreground` by default (see components/ui/card.tsx line 11). Moreover, they conflict with the `grade-surface` class on the same element, which intentionally sets its own `background-color: var(--grade-color)` and `color: var(--grade-ink)`. Adding these two utilities both duplicates the Card defaults and creates a CSS cascade conflict over the intended grade-colored surface. Per the project rules (className is for layout only; never override component colors), these should be removed.

The `.dark` block redefines the entire navy family (`--navy-deep`, `--navy-muted`, `--navy-soft`) to light cream tones, and the new `--sidebar: var(--navy-deep)` inherits that inversion. Per the brand rule "Brand surfaces (header/footer/hero) = solid navy #1e2a38, NEVER inverted in dark mode", the sidebar nav surface should stay navy in dark mode, but here it resolves to a cream surface (#fefce8) with dark foreground. Consider pinning the sidebar surface to a stable navy token that is not inverted in dark mode so the nav stays consistent with the brand rule.

This added `has-data-[slot=card-description]:grid-rows-[auto_auto]` is redundant dead code: the base class already unconditionally applies `grid-rows-[auto_auto]` on the same element, so the variant sets the exact same value and has no effect. If the intent was to give a different row template when a CardDescription is present (e.g. `auto_1fr`), that value should be used; otherwise this line should be dropped to avoid confusion.

Indexing a `as const` readonly tuple (`TILTS`) with a plain `number` index (`index` from the map, and `index % TILTS.length` is typed `number`) is a TypeScript compile error under `strict: true`: "Element implicitly has an 'any' type because expression of type 'number' can't be used to index type 'readonly [...]'." This will fail the build/type-check. Fix by declaring `TILTS` without `as const` (letting it widen to `string[]`), e.g. `const TILTS = ["-rotate-1", "rotate-1", "-rotate-2", "rotate-2"];`, or by typing the index as a finite literal union.

In this Next.js App Router project, internal navigation should use `next/link` via `<Button asChild>`, not a raw `<a href>`. Using a plain `<a>` for internal routes triggers a full page reload and loses Link prefetching instead of client-side navigation. The `StaffCard` component above correctly uses `<Link>` from next/link; this hero card should do the same for consistency.

This trailing re-export of Card/CardHeader/CardTitle/CardDescription/CardContent/CardFooter is unnecessary and unused (nothing imports these from StaffCard). These primitives are already imported from `@/components/ui/card` at the top of the file for internal use. Re-exporting them here only bloats the public API surface and risks naming collisions. Remove this line.
comments.existing_code: export { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardContent, CardFooter };

comments.content: The project root is hardcoded to an absolute Windows path (`C:/old-macdonald-had-a-school`). On any other machine or OS this script will point at a non-existent or unrelated directory, causing `os.walk` to silently scan nothing and the whole report (PRESENT/MISSING/UNREFERENCED) to be wrong or empty. Since the script lives in `scripts/`, derive the root relative to the file itself for portability, e.g. `ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))`.
`sys` is imported but never referenced anywhere in the script; remove the unused import.
`only_referenced_in_css_only_assets` is declared but never appended to or read, so it's dead state. Remove it (or actually populate it if CSS-only references should be tracked).
comments.existing_code: only_referenced_in_css_only_assets = []  # Used in CSS but may be used via background-image (these are fine)

comments.content: This Card already carries the unlayered `material-cardboard-paper` class, whose `.material-surface` sets `background-color: var(--material-color)` and `.material-cardboard-paper` sets `color: var(--theme-ink)`. Since these project CSS classes are defined outside Tailwind's `@layer utilities`, they win the cascade over the `bg-card`/`text-card-foreground` utilities, so these newly added token classes will not take effect here. If the intent is to force the card/token colors, the material classes should be removed or the background/color controlled declaratively.
comments.existing_code: <Card className="material-surface material-cardboard-paper relative mt-auto hidden lg:block bg-card text-card-foreground">
